newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh Moslems burn Israeli flags.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh Moslems burn Israeli flags.

text.p: Hundreds of Bangladeshi Moslems, angry at an Israeli woman's posters portraying the Prophet Mohammad as a pig, burned Israeli flags and marched with torches on Monday urging Dhaka residents to join a general strike.
Islamic groups have called the strike for Tuesday.
"The strike is intended to voice our strongest protest against attempts to ridicule the Prophet by blasphemous acts of an Israeli Jewish woman," said Abdul Quader Mollah of the Jamaat-e-Islami party.

Religious feelings were inflamed in Bangladesh, where nearly 90 percent of its 120 million people are Moslems, after a right-wing Jewish woman in Hebron plastered storefronts two weeks ago with posters portraying Mohammad as a pig.
"True Moslems can never tolerate the outrageous act and the devilish courage to dishonour Mohammad," said a leader of the radical Islamic Constitution Movement.
"The strike would reflect our anger...and whip up conscientiousness across the world," the Islami Oikya Jote, an Islamic council, said in a statement.
The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, and the Jatiya Party of former military ruler Hossain Mohammad Ershad backed the strike call.
"Any act against the Prophet and Islam calls for unanimous indignation and protest," BNP secretary-general Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan said.
The ruling Awami League opposes the strike, saying it is unwarranted after the Bangladesh parliament adopted a resolution condemning the blasphemy.
